Pregnancy Conception Calculator

Estimate a conception date from a due date or last menstrual period using conventional pregnancy dating intervals. The result is a calendar estimate because ovulation timing and cycle length vary from person to person. How to use this calculator

  1. Enter known date, due date or lmp, usual cycle length.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How pregnancy conception is calculated

A typical estimate places conception about 266 days before the estimated due date, or near 14 days after a 28-day-cycle LMP. A due date of October 8 corresponds to an estimated conception date around January 15.

Estimated conception≈due date−266 days, or LMP+cycle length−14 days.
A worked example

A due date of October 8 corresponds to an estimated conception date around January 15.

Assumptions & useful context

Calendar estimate; it cannot establish exact fertilization timing.

Health calculations are estimates for education. They cannot diagnose a condition or replace a clinician’s assessment. Individual needs vary, especially during pregnancy, illness and growth.

ACOG: Pregnancy dating and gestational length ↗

Frequently asked questions

Can this identify the exact conception day?

No. Ovulation and fertilization timing can vary.

Is this suitable for paternity or legal dating?

No; use appropriate clinical testing and records.
